messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Updated Automatic Differentiation API wiki page
parts:
I'm confused about what won't work with these instructions.
I don't think we should be putting up instructions that don't work!
I also don't think we should be encouraging people to check out
develop. Advanced users can sort that out for themselves or we
can mention it at the end. Too many choices up front gets confusing.

There's no installation --- it's header only, so there's only
a download. We really want to stress this.

The minimal example should compute a derivative. Something
like:

<...whatever we need to include...>

struct foo {
template <typename T>
T operator(const Eigen::Matrix<T, Eigen::Dynamic, 1>& x) {
using std::exp;
return x[0] * x[1] + exp(x[0]);
}
};

int main() {
Eigen::VectorXd x;
x << 2, 3;
Eigen::VectorXd grad_fx;
double fx = 0;
foo f;
gradient(f, x, fx, grad_fx);
std::cout << "x=" << x
<< " f(x) = " << fx
<< " d/dx f(x) = " << grad_fx
<< std::endl;
return 0;
}


Or do the same thing with vars directly, which might be
simpler for most users:

int main() {
using stan::agrad::var;
var a = 2;
var b = 3;
var fab = a * b + exp(a);
stan::agrad::grad(fx.vi_);
std::cout << "f(a,b) = " << fx.val()
<< "; d/da f(a,b) = " << a.adj()
<< "; d/db f(a,b) = " << b.adj();
stan::agrad::recover_memory();
}

then work up to the std::vector<> based grad() function
in var.hpp, and then the full-on functional.

- Bob
